title: Reports are slow
briefing: Analysts say scheduled reports are taking longer than usual. Investigate the report request path.

actions.label: Compare plans for slow queries
actions.criteria: Use when a limited set of query fingerprints gets slower after a query or index change.
actions.instructions: Compare saved query plans for the affected fingerprints and inspect the plan history.

actions.label: Inspect report reader pool waits
actions.criteria: Use when reporting requests queue before opening a reader connection.
actions.instructions: Compare reader pool queue depth and connection acquisition latency with query execution time.

actions.label: Check report scheduler lag
actions.criteria: Use when jobs start late and the delay may be in scheduling rather than execution.
actions.instructions: Compare job eligibility time with the scheduler dispatch timestamp.

fallback: Collect one job dispatch timestamp and its matching request timing breakdown.

events.text: Scheduled report duration is above 90 seconds. The alert covers total runtime only.
Reporting jobs scheduled at 11:00 did not enter the execution queue until 11:02. The delayed jobs span two query templates.

Reports acquired a worker on schedule in the execution service, but all waits occurred inside its shared reader pool. The scheduler dispatch event records acknowledgement after the worker acquires a reader.

debrief.summary: A connection pool queue delayed acknowledgement of dispatch. Once a report acquired a connection, its database execution time was normal.
lessons: Check what a dispatch timestamp records before interpreting the gap as scheduler delay.
Compare database query duration with the wait to acquire a connection.
